title: censor_shutdown vs concurrent worker threads: unguarded g_host race, poison-reset window, null-callback call
description: Three facets of one missing shutdown contract (arch+security audits 2026-06-12). (1) g_host is a plain static struct (censor_plugin.cpp:36) read by censor_log (:50-53) and fire_fatal (:80-81) — documented 'safe from any thread' — while censor_shutdown (:119-127) does g_host = {} with no synchronization: torn read of a function pointer = UB/crash. (2) A worker that wins the fire_fatal CAS but hasn't yet invoked the callback can see g_host zeroed mid-flight -> null function-pointer call. (3) shutdown unconditionally clears g_poisoned, so a poisoned session can re-init without the host knowing. Fix: snapshot callbacks under a shared_mutex (readers) / unique (shutdown); zero g_host BEFORE clearing g_poisoned; document+enforce 'all worker threads joined before censor_shutdown'. Becomes live the moment Censor-x7d lands a real BackgroundWorker.
close_reason: g_host under shared_mutex; callbacks invoked holding shared lock so shutdown's unique-lock zeroing waits for in-flight callbacks; host zeroed before poison reset. 231/231 tests incl. poison-banner suite.

title: NaN/Inf from untrusted PDF propagates through feature math — cosine comparator UB
description: Security audit 2026-06-12. feature_vector.cpp:50-158 does raw float arithmetic on ElementData bounds/stroke_width with no isfinite guards; one NaN coordinate from a crafted PDF poisons the FeatureVector. knn_classifier.cpp:31 'dot/(sqrt(na2)*sqrt(nb2))' — the zero guard does NOT catch NaN (NaN!=0.0f), so cosine returns NaN, and std::partial_sort (:92-96) with a NaN-feeding comparator violates strict weak ordering = UB (crash or corrupt classification in the Rapida process). title: [bug] KNNClassifier predict and add_example have no internal lock — concurrent BackgroundWorker reads race with ActiveLearner writes
description:
KNNClassifier stores its training data in std::vector<Example> examples_ with no mutex. BackgroundWorker calls classifier_->predict() (const, iterates examples_) from the worker thread. ActiveLearner::add_labeled_example() calls classifier_->add_example() which pushes to examples_. If ActiveLearner is called from a host/UI thread while BackgroundWorker is running, predict() iterates examples_ concurrently with add_example() pushing to it. std::vector reallocation during push_back invalidates all iterators, causing a data race (undefined behaviour). IClassifier::predict() is documented as 'the read path — safe for concurrent access' (background_worker.h:21), but KNNClassifier does not implement this guarantee.

Evidence: background_worker.h:20-21: 'the worker calls IClassifier::predict() (the read path — safe for concurrent access)'. knn_classifier.cpp:82-86: predict() iterates 'for (const auto& ex : examples_)' with no lock. knn_classifier.cpp:38-41: add_example() calls 'examples_.push_back(...)' with no lock. No mutex member in KNNClassifier (knn_classifier.h:34-43).

Suggested fix: Add a std::shared_mutex to KNNClassifier. In predict() take a shared (read) lock; in add_example() and label_counts() take an exclusive lock. This matches the IClassifier contract as stated in background_worker.h.

Found by 2026-06-11 codebase audit (design); adversarially verified 2/2.
close_reason: KNNClassifier examples_ under shared_mutex: predict/label_counts shared, add_example unique. 231/231 tests.

title: Fix thread-unsafe generate_uuid() in active_learning.cpp
description: generate_uuid() in active_learning.cpp uses shared mutable static variables: 'static std::mt19937 rng{std::random_device{}()}; static std::uniform_int_distribution<uint32_t> dist;'. std::mt19937 is not thread-safe. If store_suggestions() is called from multiple threads concurrently, there is a data race on the static RNG state. C++11 guarantees thread-safe initialization of static locals but not thread-safe access after initialization. Fix: use thread_local instead of static for the RNG (thread_local is per-thread, no synchronization needed), or protect with a mutex. The distribution object is stateless after construction so it can remain static. Note: store_suggestions() currently has no callers that run from worker threads but the BackgroundWorker design could enable this in future.
notes: REOPENED 2026-06-12: closed by stale-reaper, never fixed. Verified: active_learning.cpp:22-23 static mt19937+dist, no thread_local/mutex. Audit adds: (a) race is live once Censor-x7d pipeline lands (BackgroundWorker vs UI thread); (b) std::random_device may fall back to deterministic seed on MSVC -> UUID repeats across sessions -> pending_suggestions PRIMARY KEY insert silently returns false (callers ignore return). Fix: thread_local rng+dist; check insert_suggestion returns.
close_reason: generate_uuid rng+dist -> thread_local (per-thread random_device seeding). 231/231 tests.

title: Add test coverage for CensorDb storage layer
description: test_storage.cpp is effectively empty — 3 lines with just a gtest include. CensorDb implements 8 methods (insert_label, query_examples_by_label, count_per_class, insert_suggestion, confirm_suggestion, reject_suggestion, upsert_pattern, all_patterns) with zero test coverage. Active learning tests touch insert/confirm/reject_suggestion indirectly via :memory: db but the other 5 methods are untested. Proposal: add a free function censor::cosine_similarity(const FeatureVector&, const FeatureVector&) to censor_types.h or a new src/math_utils.h (inline, no .cpp needed). Remove the three duplicates. The active_learning variant's epsilon guard (1e-9f) and [0,1] clamping are arguably more robust — use that as the canonical implementation.

description: Headers use two inconsistent styles: #pragma once (newer, supported by all major compilers): cluster.h, spatial_clustering.h, stroke_weight_histogram.h, ceiling_grid_prepass.h, feature_vector.h, grid_system.h. #ifndef guards (traditional): censor_abi.h, censor_types.h, iclassifier.h, knn_classifier.h, active_learning.h, censor_db.h, background_worker.h, confidence_overlay.h, completeness.h, debug_viz_data.h, discovery_queue.h. Recommendation: standardize on #pragma once — simpler, no guard name collisions, all target compilers (GCC, Clang, MSVC) support it. Note: censor_abi.h is the public C header consumed by Rapida — it should keep traditional guards for maximum portability (pure C compatibility). All internal C++ headers can use #pragma once.

title: Use sqlite3_close_v2 in CensorDb::close() to handle statement leaks
description: CensorDb::close() calls sqlite3_close(db_) directly. If any sqlite3_stmt has been prepared but not finalized (e.g. due to an early return in an error path), sqlite3_close() returns SQLITE_BUSY and the handle is NOT closed, leaving db_ as a dangling pointer after 'db_ = nullptr'. The CensorDb destructor ignores the return value. sqlite3_close_v2() is the correct choice for RAII wrappers: it deregisters the handle immediately (even with open statements) and the handle is deallocated when the last prepared statement is finalized. This is standard SQLite RAII practice. Change both sqlite3_close calls in censor_db.cpp to sqlite3_close_v2.

close_reason: sqlite3_close_v2 at both sites. Clean build, 240/240 tests (VS2026 x64). Sonnet-agent implementation, reviewed + independently verified.

title: Replace placeholder .cpp files with module registration comments
description: Four source files are single-line placeholder comments: src/clustering/clustering.cpp ('// clustering module — placeholder'), src/grid/grid.cpp ('// grid module — placeholder'), src/storage/storage.cpp ('// storage module — placeholder'), src/overlay/overlay.cpp ('// overlay module — placeholder'). These are included via GLOB_RECURSE and compile to empty translation units. The real implementations are in subdirectory files (spatial_clustering.cpp, grid_system.cpp, censor_db.cpp, etc.). The placeholders add noise. Two options: (A) delete them (GLOB_RECURSE still picks up the real files), or (B) convert to module-level doc comments listing what the module contains (useful as entry points for newcomers). Recommend option A since the CLAUDE.md already documents the module layout.

title: Add default member initializers to ClusterBoundsEntry and HistogramBin
description: ClusterBoundsEntry (debug_viz_data.h) and HistogramBin (debug_viz_data.h) lack default member initializers, unlike other structs in the codebase (Cluster, CensorOverlayEntry, FeatureVector etc. all have '= {}' or '= 0' defaults). ClusterBoundsEntry: 'int cluster_id;' and 'float bounds[4];' are uninitialized. HistogramBin: 'float low; float high; int count;' are all uninitialized. In current code, get_cluster_bounds() and compute_histogram() always fully initialize before use so there's no active bug, but it's inconsistent with the rest of the codebase and fragile. Fix: add '= {}' / '= 0' defaults to all members, consistent with how Cluster and CensorOverlayEntry are defined.
